text: Replace pointwise BCE with within-user pairwise BPR while retaining the factorization-machine architecture, user/item IDs, request-context fields, split, and evaluation protocol.
rationale: The current scorer reaches GAUC 0.66891 and nDCG@5 0.53696, but the objective is ranking; pairwise training directly optimizes positive-over-negative ordering.
exact_ablation: Ablate pointwise BCE training and use one sampled positive-negative pairwise BPR loss per eligible user, leaving model, features, split, and evaluation unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase approximately 0.003 to 0.010 by improving within-user positive-versus-negative ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase approximately 0.002 to 0.008, with potentially larger gains for users whose current top-five retrieval is weak.

text: Use a within-user listwise softmax loss over each impression group instead of BCE, retaining the current factorization-machine scorer and request-context features.
rationale: The official objective averages within-user ranking metrics, while current training is pointwise; listwise normalization should better allocate probability mass toward relevant items.
exact_ablation: Ablate pointwise BCE and replace it with a numerically stable within-user listwise softmax ranking loss, with all features and architecture fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase approximately 0.002 to 0.008 through better group-relative ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase approximately 0.004 to 0.012 because listwise pressure targets the top of each user's ranking.

text: Add a bounded recent-history user representation built only from events preceding each target impression, while retaining the current factorization-machine scorer and request-context fields.
rationale: Static IDs and request context produce strong global results but leave substantial ranking failures in some groups; temporally valid recent behavior can personalize ordering beyond a static user embedding.
exact_ablation: Ablate the absence of sequential history by adding only the preceding user's last 20 impression IDs and labels, truncated before the target timestamp; keep all existing features, loss, and architecture otherwise fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase approximately 0.004 to 0.012, especially for users with sufficient prior activity.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase approximately 0.003 to 0.010 through more personalized top-five choices; cold users may see no gain.

text: Increase the factorization-machine embedding dimension from 16 to 32 while keeping the current feature set, BCE loss, optimizer, split, and evaluation fixed.
rationale: The current FM improves the additive scaffold to GAUC 0.66891 and nDCG@5 0.53696, indicating useful interactions; doubling capacity may capture additional user-context and user-item structure.
exact_ablation: Ablate the 16-dimensional interaction embedding and use a 32-dimensional embedding, changing no features, loss, optimizer, or stopping rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase approximately 0.001 to 0.005 if the current interaction representation is capacity-limited.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase approximately 0.001 to 0.006, with risk of overfitting sparse context categories.

text: Replace the factorization-machine scorer with a cross network that explicitly models low-order feature crosses, retaining the same encoded user/item and request-context inputs and BCE training.
rationale: Request context has positive screening lift of 0.00221, while several context slices remain weak; explicit crosses may model user-context and item-context effects more selectively than a single FM interaction space.
exact_ablation: Ablate the FM interaction term and replace it with one second-order cross-network layer over the same input fields, leaving feature inputs, BCE, split, and evaluation unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase approximately 0.002 to 0.008 if explicit crosses resolve context-specific ordering errors.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase approximately 0.002 to 0.009, potentially helping the weakest tab slices.

text: Add only the impression date as a categorical feature to the current factorization-machine scorer, retaining user/item IDs, tab, hourmin, weekday, BCE, and all training settings.
rationale: Request-context screening shows positive daily lifts ranging from 0.00067 to 0.00913, suggesting temporal drift that a weekday field alone may not capture.
exact_ablation: Ablate the absence of date by adding one categorical impression-date field, with every other feature, model, loss, split, and evaluation setting fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase approximately 0.0005 to 0.004 by absorbing short-term temporal drift.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase approximately 0.0005 to 0.004, though date memorization may provide limited within-day ranking value.

text: Add the known-at-request server display dimensions as categorical fields to the current factorization-machine scorer, leaving all other inputs and training unchanged.
rationale: The current context-augmented model still has poor ranking in tab 8 and hour 3; device or display context may explain residual presentation-dependent preferences without using outcomes.
exact_ablation: Ablate the absence of server_width and server_height by adding only these two impression-time categorical fields; keep architecture, loss, existing features, and evaluation fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase approximately 0.0005 to 0.004 if display context explains residual within-user preference differences.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase approximately 0.0005 to 0.005, with the largest possible effect in weak context slices.

text: Add the impression-time visible-status field to the current factorization-machine scorer while retaining all existing features, pointwise BCE training, and evaluation.
rationale: The current model has strong global ranking but very low GAUC in selected tabs, suggesting that availability or presentation-state distinctions may be missing from the scorer.
exact_ablation: Ablate the absence of visible_status by adding only the impression-time visible-status categorical field, with no other feature or training changes.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase approximately 0.0005 to 0.004 if visibility state separates otherwise-confounded impressions.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase approximately 0.0005 to 0.005 through improved candidate ordering in affected contexts.

text: Train the current factorization-machine scorer with inverse-frequency weighting for rare items, while keeping the feature set, BCE form, architecture, and validation protocol fixed.
rationale: The rare-item slice has GAUC 0.60000 and nDCG@5 0.17174 versus global GAUC 0.66891 and nDCG@5 0.53696, indicating a concentrated sparse-item weakness.
exact_ablation: Ablate uniform row weighting and weight each BCE row by a capped inverse training item-frequency factor, leaving model, features, split, and evaluation unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase approximately 0.001 to 0.007, primarily by improving rare-item ordering, with uncertain global impact.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase approximately 0.001 to 0.006 on the global metric, with a potentially larger rare-item slice gain.

text: Use separate factorization-machine interaction embeddings for user-item interactions and user-request-context interactions, while preserving the same safe feature fields and BCE training.
rationale: The request-context group has measured positive lift, yet tab 8 and tab 3 remain weak; disentangling interaction types may prevent item-context effects from competing with user-context personalization.
exact_ablation: Ablate the single shared FM interaction space and replace it with two interaction spaces, one restricted to user-item pairs and one restricted to user-request-context pairs; keep inputs, BCE, and split fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase approximately 0.002 to 0.009 if the current shared interaction representation causes interference.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase approximately 0.002 to 0.010, especially in context slices with low current ranking quality.

text: Add a small auxiliary head predicting the known-at-training user activity category while retaining the long-view head as the only scored output.
rationale: Activity segments differ materially, including GAUC 0.63628 for low_active and 0.68256 for middle_active; an auxiliary activity objective may regularize user representations without changing ranking labels.
exact_ablation: Ablate single-task long-view BCE and add one auxiliary user_active_degree classification head with fixed small loss weight, while retaining the long-view head and all existing features.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase approximately 0.001 to 0.006 by improving representation stability across activity regimes.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase approximately 0.001 to 0.006, with possible degradation if auxiliary activity prediction dominates personalization.

text: Use a two-tower user-context and item tower with a dot-product scorer instead of the current single factorization-machine scorer, retaining the same safe categorical inputs and pointwise BCE training.
rationale: The current FM provides GAUC 0.66891 and nDCG@5 0.53696, but its weakest tabs have both poor GAUC and nDCG; a structured user-context/item decomposition offers a distinct capacity bias for personalization.
exact_ablation: Ablate the single FM scorer and replace it with separate user-context and item towers whose dot product produces the long-view score; keep the same safe fields, BCE, split, and evaluation unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase approximately 0.001 to 0.008 if tower separation improves generalization of user-context preference.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase approximately 0.002 to 0.009, but may decline for rare items because cross-item memorization is reduced.
